name_note: GTDB splits the classical genus Blautia; g__Blautia_A is one of those parts and also holds genomes that NCBI labels Ruminococcus or Mediterraneibacter.

sentences.text: Blautia is a genus of anaerobic bacteria found widely in the faeces and intestines of mammals, including humans.
Several species once placed in Clostridium or Ruminococcus were reclassified into Blautia, so the limits of the genus have shifted as species were renamed.
Blautia wexlerae, a member of the genus, accumulates amylopectin and produces succinate, lactate and acetate, with distinctive amino-acid metabolism.
Studies have associated more intestinal Blautia with reduced death from graft-versus-host disease, and less Blautia with obesity and type 2 diabetes.
Depletion of Blautia species, in particular Blautia luti and B. wexlerae, has been reported in the gut microbiota of children with obesity.
